title: How an Excavator Works in 60 Seconds 🚜💪 #shorts
description:
An excavator digs with liquid, not muscle. A diesel engine spins hydraulic pumps that push oil at around 4,500 psi into cylinders on the boom, stick and bucket, while hydraulic motors swing the cab a full 360 degrees and drive each track. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#excavator #hydraulics #howitworks

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: A mid-size excavator's bucket can dig with about *18 tons* of force. And it does it with *oil*.

steps.label: Pump
steps.text: A *diesel engine* spins hydraulic pumps that squeeze oil to about *4,500 psi*.

steps.label: Cylinders
steps.text: That oil pushes pistons in *three cylinders*: one for the boom, one for the stick, one for the bucket.

steps.label: Dig
steps.text: The joysticks open valves, so oil flows in, and the arm *curls and scoops* like an elbow and wrist.

steps.label: Swing
steps.text: A hydraulic motor turns a big gear ring, so the whole cab can *swing 360 degrees*.

steps.label: Tracks
steps.text: Each track has its *own motor*. Run them opposite ways and the machine *spins in place*.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Pump, push, *dig*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
